group.passage: In September 2011, workers began tearing down two old dams on the Elwha River in Washington State, in what became the largest dam removal in U.S. history. Below, a river ecologist and a farmer who lives below another old dam give their views.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: A River Ecologist’s Column
passage_parts.text: When the Elwha Dam began producing power in 1913, it helped a young town grow and kept a pulp mill running. It also cut a river in two. A state law of 1890 required dams to let fish pass, yet the builder ignored it, and a second, taller dam followed upstream in 1927. Salmon returning from the sea were left with about five miles of river. The dams also held back sand and gravel, so spawning beds downstream wore away and the beach at the river mouth eroded. Taking the dams out reopened more than 70 miles of habitat, and within months salmon were spawning inside the national park for the first time in a century. Summer steelhead, once thought lost, have come back. The work is not finished, and some fish are returning more slowly than others. But the Elwha proves that an old dam is not a law of nature. Where a dam’s benefits no longer outweigh what it costs a river, removing it deserves a serious look.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: A Farmer’s Letter
passage_parts.text: I grow vegetables in a valley below an old dam, and in dry summers its reservoir is what keeps our fields alive. So when people hold up the Elwha as proof that dams should come down, I ask them to read the whole story. Before any concrete was broken there, $79 million was spent on water plants to protect a nearby city’s water supply from the mud stored behind the dams. Once that mud was let go, the river ran so thick with it that the number of tiny creatures young fish feed on dropped sharply for a while. Years later, Chinook salmon are still doing worse than planners had hoped, and full recovery is expected to take decades. I have nothing against salmon. I only ask that the people who depend on a dam be heard first, and that their water be secured before anyone picks up a hammer.

questions.stem: On which of the following points would both writers most likely agree?

options.A: Every old dam where salmon once swam should be taken down.
options.B: The Elwha project was a mistake because it cost too much.
options.C: The fish of the Elwha have not yet fully recovered.
options.D: People living near a dam should have the final say about removing it.

questions.stem: According to Text A, which of the following is true?

options.A: The dams were built even though a law already required a way for fish to get past.
options.B: The taller of the two dams was the first one built, in 1913.
options.C: The dams left returning salmon with about 70 miles of river.
options.D: Salmon took several decades to spawn in the park after the dams came down.

questions.stem: Why does the writer of Text B mention the $79 million spent on water plants?

options.A: To argue that the money should have been given to farmers instead.
options.B: To show that removing a dam can bring costs beyond the removal itself.
options.C: To suggest that the nearby city’s water is no longer safe to use.
options.D: To praise the planners for protecting the city’s water supply.

questions.stem: How would the writer of Text A most likely answer the farmer’s point about the mud?

options.A: The mud never reached the lower part of the river.
options.B: The farmer is right that the Elwha has not recovered at all.
options.C: Removing only the smaller dam would have kept the river clear.
options.D: The mud was a passing cost, since sand and gravel were what the river below the dams had been missing.

1.explanation_zh: Text A 說工作還沒完成，有些魚回來得比其他魚慢；Text B 說多年後奇努克鮭的情況仍不如規劃者的期望，完全恢復預計要數十年。兩人都承認艾爾瓦河的魚還沒有完全恢復，所以選 C。
evidence: The work is not finished, and some fish are returning more slowly than others.
Years later, Chinook salmon are still doing worse than planners had hoped, and full recovery is expected to take decades.

option_notes_zh.A: 過度概括：Text A 只說當水壩的好處不再大於它對河川的代價時，拆除值得認真考慮，並沒有說每一座都該拆；Text B 更不會同意。
option_notes_zh.B: Text B 只是提醒拆壩有額外成本，沒有說這個計畫是錯的；Text A 則把它當成成功的例子。
option_notes_zh.D: 以偏概全且過度推論：Text B 只要求先聽取依賴水壩的人的意見，沒有說他們有最後決定權；Text A 也沒有表示同意。

A: Where a dam’s benefits no longer outweigh what it costs a river, removing it deserves a serious look.
B: But the Elwha proves that an old dam is not a law of nature.
D: I only ask that the people who depend on a dam be heard first, and that their water be secured before anyone picks up a hammer.

1.strategy_zh: 雙文本的「共同看法」題，先各用一句話寫下兩人的立場，再找兩篇都有證據的選項。只符合其中一篇（A 偏向拆壩、D 偏向農民）或把語氣說得更強（every、final say、mistake）的選項都不能選。
hints: Text A 最後幾句承認了什麼還沒完成？
Text B 怎麼描述奇努克鮭的情況？
哪個選項在兩篇裡都找得到依據？

2.explanation_zh: Text A 說 1890 年的州法要求水壩必須讓魚能通過，但建造者不予理會；也就是說，這兩座水壩是在法律已有規定的情況下仍然建成、沒有魚道，所以選 A。
evidence: A state law of 1890 required dams to let fish pass, yet the builder ignored it, and a second, taller dam followed upstream in 1927.

option_notes_zh.B: 細節錯置：1913 年開始發電的是 Elwha Dam；比較高的第二座水壩是 1927 年才在上游建成。
option_notes_zh.C: 數字錯置：水壩讓洄游的鮭魚只剩大約五英里的河段；70 英里是拆壩後重新開放的棲地。
option_notes_zh.D: 與原文相反：拆壩後幾個月內，鮭魚就在國家公園裡產卵，是一百年來第一次。

B: When the Elwha Dam began producing power in 1913, it helped a young town grow and kept a pulp mill running.
A state law of 1890 required dams to let fish pass, yet the builder ignored it, and a second, taller dam followed upstream in 1927.
C: Salmon returning from the sea were left with about five miles of river.
Taking the dams out reopened more than 70 miles of habitat, and within months salmon were spawning inside the national park for the first time in a century.
D: Taking the dams out reopened more than 70 miles of habitat, and within months salmon were spawning inside the national park for the first time in a century.

2.strategy_zh: 細節題遇到數字，要分清楚它屬於哪一件事：five miles（建壩後剩下的河段）和 70 miles（拆壩後重新開放的棲地）；1913（第一座）和 1927（第二座、較高）。
hints: 1890 年的州法規定了什麼？建造者怎麼做？
1913 年開始發電的是哪一座水壩？
five miles 和 70 miles 各指什麼？

3.explanation_zh: Text B 的作者請大家「讀完整個故事」，接著舉例：在拆除任何混凝土之前，就先花了 7,900 萬美元蓋淨水設施，保護附近城市的供水不受壩後淤泥影響。作者提這筆錢，是要說明拆壩不只是拆掉水壩本身，還會帶來其他成本，所以選 B。
evidence: So when people hold up the Elwha as proof that dams should come down, I ask them to read the whole story.
Before any concrete was broken there, $79 million was spent on water plants to protect a nearby city’s water supply from the mud stored behind the dams.

option_notes_zh.A: 文中沒有說這筆錢應該改給農民；作者只要求先聽取依賴水壩的人的意見、確保他們的用水。
option_notes_zh.C: 與原文相反：這些設施是為了保護城市的供水才蓋的，作者沒有說城市的水不能用。
option_notes_zh.D: 正確但答非所問：設施確實是為了保護供水，但作者提它不是為了稱讚規劃者，而是要指出拆壩的額外代價。

A: I only ask that the people who depend on a dam be heard first, and that their water be secured before anyone picks up a hammer.
C: Before any concrete was broken there, $79 million was spent on water plants to protect a nearby city’s water supply from the mud stored behind the dams.
D: So when people hold up the Elwha as proof that dams should come down, I ask them to read the whole story.
Before any concrete was broken there, $79 million was spent on water plants to protect a nearby city’s water supply from the mud stored behind the dams.

3.strategy_zh: 目的題要看例子前面的主張：I ask them to read the whole story 表示接下來要補充「故事的另一面」，7,900 萬美元就是這另一面的第一個例子。
hints: 作者在提到這筆錢之前，請大家做什麼？
這筆錢是在拆壩之前還是之後花的？用來做什麼？
作者想讓讀者注意拆壩的哪一面？

4.explanation_zh: Text A 說水壩攔住了砂石，導致下游的產卵河床被沖刷掉、河口的海灘被侵蝕，可見在他看來，下游缺少的正是被攔住的砂石。農民指出淤泥放出後河水混濁、小生物一度大減；Text A 的作者最可能回應：這是暫時的代價，因為這些砂石正是下游一直缺少、可以修補河床與海灘的東西。所以選 D。
evidence: The dams also held back sand and gravel, so spawning beds downstream wore away and the beach at the river mouth eroded.
Once that mud was let go, the river ran so thick with it that the number of tiny creatures young fish feed on dropped sharply for a while.

option_notes_zh.A: 與原文相反：Text B 說淤泥放出後河水變得很混濁，Text A 也沒有否認淤泥流到下游。
option_notes_zh.B: 與 Text A 相反：Text A 說鮭魚幾個月內就在國家公園產卵、夏季虹鱒也回來了，不會同意河川「完全沒有恢復」；Text B 也沒有這樣說。
option_notes_zh.C: 文中沒有提到只拆較小的水壩能讓河水保持清澈。

A: Once that mud was let go, the river ran so thick with it that the number of tiny creatures young fish feed on dropped sharply for a while.
B: Taking the dams out reopened more than 70 miles of habitat, and within months salmon were spawning inside the national park for the first time in a century.
Summer steelhead, once thought lost, have come back.
C: A state law of 1890 required dams to let fish pass, yet the builder ignored it, and a second, taller dam followed upstream in 1927.

4.strategy_zh: 跨文本推論題：先找 Text A 對「砂石」的看法（被攔住是問題，造成河床與海灘流失），再用這個立場回應 Text B 的抱怨（淤泥一度造成傷害）。和兩篇原文相反、或兩篇都沒提到的選項先排除。
hints: Text A 說水壩攔住砂石造成了什麼問題？
Text B 說淤泥放出後發生了什麼事？持續多久？
以 Text A 的立場，被放出的砂石是好事還是壞事？

translation_zh.text:
2011 年 9 月，工人開始拆除美國華盛頓州艾爾瓦河上的兩座舊水壩，這後來成為美國史上規模最大的拆壩工程。以下是一位河川生態學者和一位住在另一座舊水壩下游的農民的看法。
【A　河川生態學者的專欄】Elwha 水壩在 1913 年開始發電時，幫助一座年輕的城鎮成長，也讓一座紙漿廠得以運轉。但它也把一條河切成兩半。1890 年的州法要求水壩必須讓魚通過，建造者卻置之不理；1927 年，上游又蓋了第二座、更高的水壩。從海洋洄游的鮭魚只剩下大約五英里的河段。水壩也攔住了砂石，於是下游的產卵河床被沖刷殆盡，河口的海灘也遭到侵蝕。拆除水壩後，重新開放了超過 70 英里的棲地，幾個月內，鮭魚就在國家公園裡產卵，這是一百年來的第一次。曾被認為已經消失的夏季虹鱒也回來了。工作還沒有完成，有些魚回來得比其他魚慢。但艾爾瓦河證明，舊水壩並不是自然法則。當一座水壩帶來的好處不再大於它對河川造成的代價時，拆除它值得認真考慮。
【B　一位農民的投書】我在一座舊水壩下游的山谷種菜，在乾燥的夏天，是它的水庫讓我們的田保持生機。所以當有人拿艾爾瓦河當作水壩應該拆除的證據時，我請他們把整個故事讀完。在那裡，連一塊混凝土都還沒敲掉之前，就先花了 7,900 萬美元蓋淨水設施，保護附近一座城市的供水不受壩後淤泥影響。淤泥一放出來，河水混濁不堪，幼魚賴以為食的小生物數量一度大幅減少。多年後，奇努克鮭的情況仍不如規劃者的期望，完全恢復預計要花上數十年。我並不反對鮭魚。我只是要求：先聽聽依賴水壩的人的意見，並在任何人拿起鐵鎚之前，確保他們的用水。

open_tasks.prompt: Compare the two writers. For each text, write one English sentence stating the writer’s view on removing old dams and one piece of evidence the writer gives.
reference_answers: Text A: Old dams that cost a river more than they give should be considered for removal; after the Elwha dams came down, salmon spawned in the national park within months.
Text B: Dam removal should wait until the people who depend on a dam are heard and their water is secured; the Elwha project needed $79 million in water plants before the dams were removed.
checklist_zh: 兩篇各寫出作者對拆除舊水壩的看法
兩篇各舉出一項文中的證據
看法和證據有沒有對應到正確的一篇
